requirement:
Every `ripgrep` or `ast_grep` excerpt, including matching and context text,
MUST be clipped to
the source span of the outline item identified by their `file` and `item`,
including that item's attached source under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Clipping MUST apply within a line shared by different items.
rationale:
I judged this from the two supplied tests in `src/authoring/tools.rs` and did not request any implementation source.

**Obligations derived from `requirements.authoring.search_accounting.excerpts`:**
1. Every `ripgrep` and `ast_grep` excerpt, both matching and context text, is clipped to the source span of the item named by `file` and `item`.
2. That span includes the item's attached source under `requirements.references.outline_comments`: doc comments, attributes and trailing comment runs.
3. Clipping applies within a line shared by different items.

**Coverage by `search_excerpts_stop_at_byte_boundaries_including_attached_comments_and_attributes`** (marked `{test}` for the subject):
- **Neighbouring lines:** the file has `fn before`, `fn after` and `fn last` next to `fn target`. `ripgrep` runs with `context:99`, which would pull in neighbouring lines if clipping failed. The test asserts that `unwanted_before`, `unwanted_after`, `unwanted_last` and `fn last` appear nowhere in the output. This covers context clipping.
- **Both tools:** the loop runs `ripgrep` and `ast_grep` and makes the same assertions on each. Each returns exactly three matches, with items `fn[target]`, `fn[left]` and `fn[right]`.
- **Attached source:** for `ripgrep`, the `fn[target]` excerpt must contain the `/// needle docs` doc comment and the `#[inline]` attribute. The `fn[right]` excerpt must contain `#[inline] fn right`. The `fn[left]` excerpt must contain the trailing block comment `needle attached`. This covers the "attached source" clause, including the rule that a comment after other source on the same line belongs to the innermost item.
- **Shared line:** `fn left`, a comment, `#[inline]`, `fn right` and `fn last` all sit on one line. The test asserts that the `fn[left]` excerpt lacks `fn right`, the `fn[right]` excerpt lacks `fn left` and `needle attached`, and nothing leaks `fn last`. This covers clipping within a shared line in both directions.
- **Byte boundaries:** the multibyte `café` is checked, and a `café` search with `context:0` yields only `fn[target]`.
- **Attribute-only match:** a search for `inline` returns exactly `fn[target]` and `fn[right]`.

**Coverage by `exact_match_ranges_preserve_regex_anchors_and_skip_unmatched_or_binary_sources`** (marked `{test}` for the subject):
- With `context:10` and several anchored patterns, the excerpt is exactly the single line `fn exact() { needle(); }`. The following `fn last() {}` is excluded, so context is clipped to the item.
- This is a supporting check for `ripgrep` clipping.

**Gaps:** I found none. Plausible violations would be unclipped context, neighbouring items leaking on a shared line, or attached comments and attributes omitted or misassigned. The assertions above would catch each of these for both tools. Nothing here is delegated to a refining requirement, and there are no acknowledgments.

text: :::{req} search_accounting.excerpts
Every `ripgrep` or `ast_grep` excerpt, including matching and context text,
MUST be clipped to
the source span of the outline item identified by their `file` and `item`,
including that item's attached source under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Clipping MUST apply within a line shared by different items.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. Habeas MUST retain the
one-based line and UTF-8 byte column of each inline role’s opening brace or
fenced reference’s first opening colon. When siblings share a line, the
reference belongs to the item owning the comment at that position. A reference
in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
